number.why: The served HR 0.70 with 95% CI 0.61–0.82 matches the cardiovascular composite for atorvastatin versus placebo after median follow-up of 5.9 years. Confirmation applies to the reported HR; it does not establish the outcome metadata's RR or intention-to-treat label. The ruling already identifies both limitations.

quotes.span: a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction or stroke, or coronary revascularization (to assess effects on major cardiovascular events)

After a median of 5.9 years, a primary cardiovascular event had occurred in 297 participants (10.9 events per 1000 person-years) in the atorvastatin group and in 412 participants (15.5 events per 1000 person-years) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.70; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.61 to 0.82; P<0.001).
Analyses were performed according to a hierarchical testing plan.

entry.why: The randomized entry population explicitly consists of community-dwelling adults aged at least 70 without cardiovascular disease, satisfying the question's age and primary-prevention criteria. Excluding diabetes and dementia further narrows this eligible population without contradicting those criteria.

quotes.span: Community-dwelling adults at least 70 years of age with no history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or dementia were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive atorvastatin at a dose of 40 mg once daily or identical placebo.

missed: No additional finding in the supplied sources changes either judgment.
